payload.statement: Collier, Monk, Maini and Lewis (1996) construct a two-state contact-mediated lateral-inhibition model in which receipt of Notch activation reduces Delta production, and report that this feedback can amplify differences between adjacent cells into a pattern.
payload.title: Source assertion: Collier 1996 propose that Delta-Notch lateral inhibition with feedback can generate fine-grained cell-state patterns

limitations: Not evaluated; the cited experiments were not read.

payload.statement: Integrating the ODEs in BioModels file BIOMD0000001047 (sha256 da21ab52...) as written, with its stored non-dimensional parameters (a=0.01, b=100, h=2, k=2, mu=1, rho=1), the symmetric steady state has a positive Jacobian eigenvalue, and from the file's initial conditions (cell 2 starts 1% below cell 1) the two cells end in opposite Delta/Notch states.
payload.title: Model behaviour: as encoded in BIOMD0000001047 the symmetric state is unstable and the file's perturbation resolves to opposite cell states

assumptions: The SBML file is as published by BioModels revision 3.

payload.context: Simulation of the two-cell Delta-Notch model as encoded in BIOMD0000001047. Non-dimensional; no organism observation; no claim about flying fish.
limitations: OpenResearch does not record the execution environment (interpreter, OS, packages, hardware); local runs use the host's own environment and container images are mutable tags, so the record alone does not say how to reproduce the environment.
Inputs outside the committed git snapshot and any random seeds are not recorded; only the command string and the committed code are.
OpenResearch does not hash or register run outputs; the content digest in this record was computed by the adapter from a mutable local run directory at retrieval time.
Run, experiment and project ids are random UUIDs local to one machine's store: there is no shared registry, and the run can be deleted by its owner (`orx exp delete`).
A run reaching status 'done' means the process exited 0. It says nothing about scientific validity and has not been reviewed.
The database exit_code was NULL for this local run; the exit code was read from the run directory's exit_code file instead.
Same author wrote the model replay and ran this capture: this is a repeat, not independent replication.
The independent evaluator in the controls reads the same SBML file.
The run fetched the SBML over the network; its digest is verified against BioModels' declared hash, but orx does not record that input.
Fidelity of the file to the paper was not checked (paper full text not read).
Does not bear on any flying-fish tissue.
payload.method: Local OpenResearch run of `python3 run_replay.py`, which fetches BIOMD0000001047 from BioModels (sha256-verified), runs the libroadrunner replay with its controls, and writes out/receipt.json and four output files. A second execution of the same code, not a different method: its outputs were compared byte-for-byte with the receipt committed in delphi-frontier.
